subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files as part of the core bootstrap context contract, and should that contract be global, exact-session scoped, or deferred to a broader context API?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but broadening startup context injection creates a public config and prompt-surface contract in an area where repository policy treats config and session-state behavior as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow explicit in-workspace custom basenames through the existing bootstrap-extra-files path after the linked PR or a replacement is repaired, documented, and tested against path guards, budgets, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and close or redirect the custom-file requests to narrower first-class filename or workspace-convention proposals.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context API
options.body: Keep the issue open only as design input if maintainers want a larger context or capability API rather than raw configured files.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow explicit in-workspace custom basenames through the existing bootstrap-extra-files path after the linked PR or a replacement is repaired, documented, and tested against path guards, budgets, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged the original hook work and later refactored the boundary-safe loader path, making them the strongest available routing owner for the config/context contract decision.
